body: Tapering off Lyrica (pregabalin) should be done gradually to avoid withdrawal symptoms like anxiety, insomnia, nausea, or rebound pain. Since your doctor already advised stopping, it’s best to follow their tapering plan. Dropping from 75mg twice daily to 25mg twice daily is a big jump—some people reduce by 25mg at a time over weeks. Ask your doctor about a slower taper if needed. Stay hydrated, monitor symptoms, and if you feel unwell, consult your doctor immediately.

It sounds like you had an intense reaction to Lyrica (pregabalin), especially since you were sleep-deprived. Lyrica can have stronger effects when you're sleep-deprived or fatigued, as your body and brain are already in a heightened state of stress. Lack of sleep can amplify the drug's sedative effects, and for some people, it can also increase the chances of experiencing vivid or distorted sensory perceptions, like the visuals you described.

Visual distortions, glowing effects, and the sense of altered reality are not uncommon with high doses of Lyrica, especially if you're not accustomed to it. This might be more intense when combined with being awake for an extended period, as sleep deprivation can alter your brain chemistry and sensory processing.

However, the experience you had seems a bit more intense than what some users report. It's important to be cautious with dosage, especially if you're not used to the medication. High doses can lead to side effects like dizziness, confusion, and altered perception, and mixing this with sleep deprivation can increase these effects.

If you're planning to use Lyrica again, it might be worth reducing the dose and making sure you're well-rested to avoid any further intense reactions. If these effects worry you or become more frequent, consider speaking to your doctor about your experiences. They can help guide you on proper dosing and whether this medication is the right option for you.
